summary: Every public address is behind Microsoft's sign-in, with fewer rights behind it.

new.title: The MCP server is behind Microsoft's sign-in
new.text: Like the web app, the MCP server now answers only requests that carry a valid Microsoft sign-in. It still checks the token and the person's role itself.

new.title: Every public address is checked
new.text: Each update lists every part of the installation that is reachable from the internet and reports any that is not behind Microsoft's sign-in.

fixes.title: The web app verifies who signed in
fixes.text: With Microsoft's sign-in, the web app takes the person only from a sign-in token it verifies itself, never from a header alone.

fixes.title: No Key Vault access for the web app
fixes.text: The web app keeps its sign-in keys in its own storage, so it no longer holds any right on the Key Vault.

fixes.title: The updater only reads group membership
fixes.text: The updater no longer holds the right to change group memberships. It only checks that the database job's membership is in place and says when it is not.

fixes.title: Leftovers of the earlier sign-in are removed
fixes.text: After the switch, the earlier sign-in's settings and its database tables are removed, each step read back. Anything else is reported.

fixes.title: A refused save says who refused it
fixes.text: When a save is refused, the message now says whether SecurityInsight or the sign-in layer refused it, and what to do.
